decision_summary.text: Whether to accept a time-limited second-site program while defining which operational imperfections can be carried.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: The pilot would need an honest duration, a clear decision date, and a credible promise about what happens to participants if it ends.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I am leaning toward accepting a four-month, twice-monthly program at Willow Hub, but only if we recruit one named site coordinator and finish the first version of the drop-in curriculum before launch.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: You could define what “ready enough” means in terms of what a participant and volunteer must be able to do, rather than whether every planned material is finished.

threads.text: Whether the curriculum condition will become another movable reason to delay expansion.

introduced.speaker: user
introduced.quote: My volunteer lead thinks those conditions are reasonable, although she worries the curriculum requirement will become another delay.

constraints.text: The current site has variable attendance and fragile volunteer coverage.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: But our current site is inconsistent: some nights we have thirty participants, some nights twelve, and volunteer coverage is fragile.

constraints.text: Participants' shift work and care duties make irregular attendance normal.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Participants work shifts, care for relatives, and come when they can.

constraints.text: Willow Hub can provide a room and promotion but cannot promise staff coordination.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Willow Hub can give us a room and promote the sessions. I had been talking as if they would also coordinate locally, but their director clarified that they cannot promise staff time. Our volunteer lead still wants to do it. She says new volunteers are more likely to join something that feels like growth than something described as fixing operations. I partly agree, and I partly think we are using inspiration to avoid the unglamorous work.

constraints.text: The volunteer lead believes growth-oriented work will attract more volunteers.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: She says new volunteers are more likely to join something that feels like growth than something described as fixing operations.

constraints.text: A foundation officer informally said geographic reach may make the application easier to explain; no funding was promised.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: There is funding context too. A foundation officer told me informally that geographic reach would make our next application easier to explain. She did not promise anything, and the current grant pays for curriculum improvement, not expansion. If we delay, we can improve the drop-in materials and volunteer training. If we expand, we have a stronger story but might be stretching restricted work into the background. I am embarrassed by how much the application narrative is affecting me.

constraints.text: The current grant funds curriculum improvement, not expansion.

constraints.text: Current volunteers report that twice-monthly scheduling may be harder rather than easier.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: That sounds like a pilot, but our current volunteers say irregular scheduling is harder, not easier.

constraints.text: Participants may treat an advertised pilot as permanent even when its schedule is limited.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Participants may also assume it is permanent once we advertise it.

constraints.text: Willow Hub needs an answer within three weeks for calendar planning.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: The community center wants an answer within three weeks because they are planning their calendar.
